title: Rational descent of the zeta series
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$,
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically connected
of pure dimension $d$, with $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ the
smooth-proper
cohomological family.
Fix an indeterminate $T$. For $n\geq1$, put
$N_n(X_0)=\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and define the
point-count zeta series

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}N_n(X_0)\frac{T^n}{n}\right).
$$

Assume the closed-point product

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}(1-T^{\deg(x)})^{-1}
$$

and the trace-to-determinant identity

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\Ql(T).
$$

Writing
$Z(X_0,T)=\sum_{n\geq0}z_nT^n$, assume that its Hankel matrix
$\mathcal H(Z)=(z_{r+s})_{r,s\geq0}$ has finite rank, in the sense of the
Hankel-matrix definition; equivalently,
the sequence $(z_n)$ satisfies a linear recurrence over $\mathbf Q$ from
some index onward. A normalized presentation is a pair
$A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ satisfying

$$
Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T),\qquad A(0)=B(0)=1,\qquad
\gcd(A,B)=1\text{ in }\mathbf Q[T],
$$

and this is the
normalized integral-fraction
condition. Then

$$
Z(X_0,T)\in\mathbf Q(T).
$$

proof.text: By [def-weil-point-counts-zeta], the series $C(T)=Z(X_0,T)$ belongs to $1+T\mathbf Q[[T]]$, so its coefficients $z_n$ lie in $\mathbf Q$. Its Hankel matrix over $\mathbf Q$ is $(z_{r+s})_{r,s\geq0}$ by [def-weil-hankel-matrix]. The hypothesis says exactly that the ranks over $\mathbf Q$ of all its finite square submatrices have a common finite bound. Thus $C\in\mathbf Q[[T]]$ satisfies condition (2) of the rationality criterion over $K=\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Proof, specialization K = Q and identification of the finite-rank hypothesis; point-count series definition

proof.text: Apply the implication (2) $\Rightarrow$ (1) of [prop-weil-rationality-criterion] to $K=\mathbf Q$ and $C=Z(X_0,T)$ using step 1. It gives polynomials $P,Q\in\mathbf Q[T]$ with $Q(0)=1$ and $Q(T)Z(X_0,T)=P(T)$ in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$.

source.place: Proof, equivalence of the first two conditions of prop-weil-rationality-criterion

proof.text: Since $Q(0)=1\neq0$ in $\mathbf Q$, the equality $QZ=P$ from step 2 meets the defining condition for a rational power series in [def-weil-rational-power-series]. Consequently $Z(X_0,T)$ is the Taylor series of $P/Q\in\mathbf Q(T)$, which is precisely the claimed membership $Z(X_0,T)\in\mathbf Q(T)$.

source.place: Proof, final conclusion Z(X_0,T) belongs to Q(T)
